The transcript contains 34 deterministic observations: natural/warm admissions; healthy → cooling → trial → healthy progression; low-streak route decisions; three distinct recovery sessions; cache rate, sample/token counts, trial cohorts, quota counts, admission classifications, session preference/protection; nanosecond points around warm, residence, cooldown, recovery and statistics boundaries; exact 5s/30s availability boundaries. Advancing time alone does not recover health: the recovery evidence event does. Boundary exploration deliberately revisits times (including rollback); frozen and current results match for this finite sequence. UpdatedAt is excluded because the accepted design distinguishes business-change time from successful verification; version/load timestamps are also excluded. No samples, phases, rates, quotas, or admission classifications are excluded. Residence eligibility for low-cache routes is covered separately because high-cache preference can remain protected beyond residence.

This fixture uses the unchanged deterministic in-memory transaction test store, not PostgreSQL or the incremental store; it proves frozen algorithm/API observational equivalence for the event sequence. Current exact-vs-incremental differential tests separately verify the optimized store path. It does not claim arbitrary event equivalence, process crash behavior, full candidate ordering, or equivalence of deliberately changed history-capacity behavior. Source generator remains a temporary test in the frozen copy; current tests cannot regenerate the checked-in JSON.

All five algorithm files also match the independently saved `.tmp/protection-perf-baseline/upstreamcacheguard` after CRLF normalization; raw-byte SHA differences between those two frozen locations are line endings only.
